mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the next month reduces discount rates applied to corporate earnings forecasts, lowering the present value of future cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the following 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by 0.25% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during a similar rate-stable period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% while UNRATE falls by >0.2% over the next month
failure_condition: 60-day returns show no significant correlation with the labor strength signal (Pearson IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% followed by a rebound above the prior month's level indicates a turning point in supply constraints, prompting a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as demand recovers.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO drops 2% in month N then rises in month N+1
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return in the 20-day window following such a pattern (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of consumer price index to GDP (CPIAUCSL) rises above 110 for three consecutive months, it indicates accelerating inflation expectations that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, which in turn produces negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 10-year yield proxy (implied by FEDFUNDS movements) over a 3-month horizon lowers the cost of capital, increasing the present value of equities and generating positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns show no correlation with 10-year yield decline (Pearson IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% and monthly pay growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 0.5% for two consecutive months, it creates a labor market overhang that suppresses wage growth expectations and equity valuations, producing negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS grows >0.5% for 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly lower than during comparable labor market expansions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies but proxyable via HOUST for consumer activity) exceeding 2% for three months suggests resilient demand, which supports positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day returns show no significant positive response (Pearson IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the supply-side inflation pressure measured by the monthly change in the core CPIAUCSL (excluding food and energy) exceeds 0.3% for two consecutive months in a tightening cycle regime, it raises policy uncertainty and reduces equity risk appetite, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: differential(CPIAUCSL) > 0.3% for 2 months in a tightening cycle
regime_hint: tightening cycle with rising core inflation
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during similar episodes with flat core inflation (t-test p > 0.05).
